hypothesis: Iter 91 = treat calibration as the INVERSE PROBLEM it is, plus four measured bug fixes. iter-90's structural work SUCCEEDED: the embedding->physiology map became invertible (with no meal in the calibration window, calibration recovers a person's fasting glucose to 0.96 mg/dL; iter-89 was 54 mg/dL and WORSE than predicting the population mean). But it missed its criterion WITH a meal (Gb skill -1.38), and the gate regressed (glucose 0.193->0.210, hr 0.158->0.202). DIAGNOSIS (and my first hypothesis was REFUTED by my own controlled test, which is why this iter is right): I claimed per-patient meal amplitude was unsupervised, so calibration inflated Gb to fit meal peaks. I then fitted amplitude almost perfectly (peak err 0.89 mg/dL) with the setpoint heads FROZEN, and Gb recovery got WORSE (-1.47 -> -2.93). Making amplitude CORRECT did not make it IDENTIFIABLE. Re-measuring at the REAL benchmark observation density (30-min check-ins, not the 60-min my test used -- my test was itself manufacturing part of the problem) shows the model ALREADY recovers HR/SBP/DBP/HRV well (skill +0.56/+0.77/+0.91/+0.14 with NO prior). Gb is the ONLY failure. THE REAL CAUSE IS UNDERDETERMINATION: EMBEDDING_DIM was 64, but a calibration window supplies ~5 markers x ~10 check-ins ~= 50 numbers. 64 unknowns, ~50 equations => infinitely many embeddings fit the same data, which is exactly what we measure (cos(recovered, true) ~= 0 while the observations are explained). The VITALS escape it because their setpoints map DIRECTLY to the observable (HR relaxes with tau 3.3 min, so observed HR *is* HR0); glucose's map is indirect (tau 55 min + meal + counter-regulation), so glucose is where it bites. FIXES. (1) EMBEDDING_DIM 64->32 -- the size of the inverse problem. Measured: 32 dims fit patients' setpoints as well as 64 (glucose_mae 0.013 vs 0.006), so dims 33-64 were free parameters the data could never pin down. Module projections UNCHANGED, so iter-60's real fix (appetite projection 6->16) survives. (2) EmbeddingPriorSignal -- for an underdetermined problem a prior is the correct treatment, but the eval prior was a diagonal Gaussian fitted POST-HOC to whatever cloud training left behind. An L2 on the codes makes N(0,sigma^2 I) the distribution they were TRAINED to have. (3) BENCHMARK_GATE_PRIOR_WEIGHT 0->1.0 (swept: Gb skill -1.47 -> +0.21) -- honestly a GUARDRAIL, not a cure. (4) MealResponseSignal -- keeps the real fidelity gain (the student's per-patient meal response WAS wrong; teacher spread 40.7-78.0 mg/dL vs a frozen student) even though it does not fix identifiability. (5) THERMOREG PER-PATIENT SETPOINT -- the last module with a resting level and no restoring structure, the same gap CVS had until iter 89 (which fixed hr_mape 0.206->0.158 in one iter). temp is a thin-margin gate marker that over-predicts excursions. Now EVERY module with a resting level has an explicit, supervised, per-patient setpoint. BUGS. (a) MealResponseSignal probed every patient from NORM_CENTER while the teacher's reference starts at that patient's own fasting level. (b) WE SUPERVISED THE LATENT, NOT THE OBSERVABLE: the teacher's observed fasting glucose is Gb + offset, offset +0.85..+5.09 mg/dL VARYING per patient -- calibration only ever sees the observable, so supervising params.Gb injected a per-patient bias into exactly what the benchmark scores. The teacher now settles first and reports its ACTUAL level. (c) model.forward now OWNS the coupling layout (insulin_sweep hand-built it and missed iter-90's glp1 channel, killing the first iter-90 dispatch at epoch 0). (d) TEACHER CORTISOL WAS DOUBLE-DRIVEN (circadian target AND an additive ACTH term, but ACTH is itself circadian): nadir 11.75 vs physiological 3-5, ratio 2.17 vs 4-5x. Cortisol drives glucose (iter-90 C3), HR, BP and thermoreg, so the error propagated everywhere. Now ACTH-driven; measured nadir 4.17, peak 18.15, ratio 4.35. (e) TEACHER SUPPRESSED GLUCAGON/GHRELIN AT REST (absolute insulin, not above-basal) -- glucagon rested at 60.3 against its own basal of 70.
expectedEffect: ACCEPTANCE CRITERION: recovery-test skill POSITIVE **with a meal in the calibration window**, measured at the REAL 30-min observation density (iter-90 at that density: Gb -0.87, HR0 +0.56, SBP0 +0.77, DBP0 +0.91, HRV0 +0.14 with no prior). Gb is the target. Do NOT measure at 60-min sampling -- that was my test's own artifact and it manufactures an identifiability problem the real benchmark does not have. PRIMARY: Gb recovery goes positive; cos(recovered, true) rises well above 0 (it was ~0 = orthogonal, the signature of underdetermination). SECONDARY (gate): glucose_mape should IMPROVE -- the same inflated Gb that broke recovery also drove the fasting-eval prediction upward, and the prior alone cuts Gb |err| 18.5 -> 5.7. NOTE the iter-90 gate regression was probably iter-89's ARTIFACT COLLAPSING, not a real loss: with Sg 30x too weak (tau 515 min) glucose barely moved across a 690-min episode, so iter-89 'predicted' the flat fasting eval by STAYING AT ITS INITIAL CONDITION -- which IS the true value. It scored well by NOT MOVING. With tau=55 min the model finally COMMITS to a prediction and is judged on whether the calibrated Gb is right. Same species as the iter-87 meal-timing artifact. WATCH: (R1) EMBEDDING_DIM 64->32 is an architecture change -- if glp1/ghrelin regress, the iter-60 capacity worry was real after all (but the projections are unchanged, so it should not be). (R2) thermoreg setpoint adds a restoring force to a thin-margin gate marker (temp 0.0182 vs 0.02) -- it should HELP (it is the fix that took hr from 0.206 to 0.158) but watch temp. (R3) the teacher changed materially (cortisol rhythm, glucagon/ghrelin resting levels), so cold-distill targets for those markers move -- expect their MAPEs to shift and judge on PHYSIOLOGY, not on the delta. (R4) embedding_prior_weight is deliberately weak (0.001); if setpoint_supervision's per-marker MAE rises, it is too strong and is flattening per-patient information.
